title: Introducing the Open Knowledge Format (Google Cloud Blog)
snippet: Official GCP announcement of OKF v0.1 (Sam McVeety & Amir Hormati, Data Cloud), June 12/13 2026. Frames OKF as vendor-neutral markdown+YAML frontmatter format; notes Knowledge Catalog updated to ingest OKF.

credibility.basis: Official vendor primary announcement (Google Cloud); authoritative on OKF intent, vendor-bias noted.

quote: That's why today, we're introducing the Open Knowledge Format (OKF), an open specification that formalizes the LLM-wiki pattern into a portable, interoperable format. This is a vendor-neutral, agent- and human-friendly standard for representing the metadata, context, and curated knowledge that modern AI systems need. ... We have also updated Google Cloud's Knowledge Catalog to be able to ingest Open Knowledge Format and serve it to our agents.

title: knowledge-catalog/okf README (GoogleCloudPlatform)
snippet: Official OKF README. Lists intended producers (Google ADK, LangChain, export pipelines from Dataplex/Unity Catalog/Collibra) and consumers (Obsidian, Notion, MkDocs, search index, graph viewer). 'Why OKF' section enumerates what the format unlocks.

credibility.basis: Primary OKF spec/repo artifact (authoritative source; batch domain heuristic does not recognize github/pypi authority).

quote: Anyone can produce OKF — humans authoring by hand, agents built on any framework (Google ADK, LangChain, custom), export pipelines from existing catalogs (Dataplex, Unity Catalog, Collibra, ...), or scripts walking a database. Anyone can serve and consume OKF — a static file server, a knowledge-management UI (Obsidian, Notion, MkDocs), an LLM loading files into context, a search index, or a graph viewer like the one bundled in this repo.

title: OKF v0.1 SPEC.md (GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog)

title: Agent Skills Explained: SKILL.md vs MCP (DevToolLab, 2026)
snippet: Comparable format detail: Agent Skills is a folder convention (SKILL.md + files) whose entire spec is two required YAML fields plus a markdown body — structurally parallel to OKF's single-required-field minimalism.

credibility.basis: Secondary explainer / community amplification; useful context, non-primary.

quote: The reason is boring in the best way: the entire spec is two required YAML fields and a Markdown body. No JSON-RPC, no auth handshake, no server process to keep alive.
